label: group chat
lines: maya: ok that video actually broke down the internet way better than i expected 📶
dev: right, starting with wifi and routers as basically the local bridge to your isp
sam: and every device gets its own ip address, data gets chopped into packets and reassembled at the other end
maya: don't forget the undersea cables and fiber optic lines carrying all that lol, wild that isps maintain those
dev: the url-to-page part was the best bit imo. dns turns the domain name into an ip, request hits the web server
sam: then you get html, css and javascript back and the browser assembles it into the page
maya: all wrapped in https encryption plus firewalls filtering stuff, makes sense

dev: then it went through basically everything built on top - email, streaming, cloud computing, social media, e-commerce, search engines, cookies, mobile data, iot, vpns, p2p, open source, hosting, cdns 😅
sam: same plumbing under all of it which is kind of wild when you think about it
maya: and at the end it covered the actual rules - protocols like http, ftp, smtp, all riding on tcp/ip
dev: plus bandwidth and latency, security stuff like malware and phishing
sam: and net neutrality loosely enforced through standards bodies like icann, ietf and w3c
maya: solid rundown honestly, way clearer than i thought this topic could be
